scope: L1 report attribution and session completion in noble-ngraph-experiment: the hardened adapter against real CLIs in both --opt legs, compared with the retained extraction receipt, plus the rule-mutation check of the fixture-child tests.

harness.workload: B1 I1-I4; B2 10 named graphs + 64 random Core programs x 200 vectors (L2-L4), L1 on named design vectors + 24 vectors per named graph and 16 random programs x 24 vectors, I4 1000 host steps; B3 source controls

B1 I1-I4; B2 10 named graphs + 64 random Core programs x 200 vectors (L2-L4), L1 on named design vectors + 24 vectors per named graph and 16 random programs x 24 vectors, I4 1000 host steps; B3 source controls

non_claims: The checks bind reports to the submitted sequence and to the self-reported module identity; they do not attest a malicious child or prove the semantics of the pinned CLI or engine.
The fixture children and mutations are finite negative controls, not a proof of execution correctness.
A CLI-version difference is attributed by exact reproduction with a CLI built from the baseline revision; it is not explained beyond that.
